instagram.author: thatrebeccarose
instagram.body:
I know this sounds a bit ironic coming from someone who literally posts on social media!

But I’ve been thinking about this a lot recently because on one hand, social media isn’t inherently bad at all. I genuinely love it. I’ve learnt so much from it, found creators I really look up to, and I love keeping up with my friends.

But at the same time, these apps are literally designed to keep us scrolling. That’s how they make money. Think about how many times you’ve opened Instagram just to reply to one message, check a notification or post a story... and somehow 30 minutes disappear. I’ve done it so many times!

So now, before I open an app, I try to ask myself one question:

Why am I opening this?

Is it because I want to reply to a friend? Watch a few funny videos? Get some inspiration? Post something?

Or am I actually just bored, avoiding something or looking for a distraction?

I’ve realised they’re two completely different experiences.

I’ve also become way more intentional about who I follow. If someone’s content consistently leaves me comparing myself or feeling worse about my own life, I’ll mute or unfollow them. On the other hand, I love following people who genuinely inspire me, teach me something or make me laugh.

For example, if I’m looking for fashion inspiration, I’d much rather follow someone whose style + body type feels realistic for me than someone whose content just makes me feel like I’ll never measure up. I’d rather leave the app feeling inspired than insecure.

And I know we all know this already, but I still think it’s worth reminding ourselves that

Social media is a highlight reel!

Even when people are being vulnerable or “real”, it’s still a tiny, curated snapshot of their life that they have still edited + looked over multiple times before posting!! + I do exactly the same. I post the highlights of my day on my story (because i like taking pics of all the nice moments), I am obviously not going to take a picture of me crying or having a difficult conversation 20 minutes later. 

That doesn’t make social media fake, it just means it’s never the full picture! 

#socialmedia #doomscrolling #socia
